questions.scenario: A mobile application records a user's spoken question. You want to send the recording directly to a model in Microsoft Foundry and receive a text answer in a single model call.
questions.question: What should you deploy?

options.why: Correct. Audio-capable models accept audio input and return text or audio.
A text-only model cannot accept audio input.
Embedding models produce vectors and do not answer questions.
Image-generation models create images from prompts.

questions.explanation: An audio-capable multimodal model can interpret a spoken prompt directly.

questions.question: When you send audio to an audio-capable model by using the Chat Completions message format, which content part type carries the recording?

options.why: Correct. The input_audio part contains base64-encoded audio data and its format.
file_search is an agent tool, not a message content part.
SSML is markup for speech synthesis in Azure Speech.

questions.explanation: Audio is sent as an input_audio content part with base64 data and a format such as wav.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about responding to spoken prompts are true?

options.text: An audio-capable model can return a response as audio as well as text.
options.why: Correct. You can request text and audio output modalities.

options.text: A pipeline of speech to text, a text model and text to speech is an alternative approach.
options.why: Correct. The pipeline chains three steps and exposes a transcript at each stage.

options.text: Audio input bypasses the content filters configured on the deployment.
options.why: Guardrails apply to audio prompts and responses as well.

options.text: Audio must be sent to the model as a local file path.
options.why: The model cannot read local paths. The audio is sent as base64 data.

questions.explanation: Audio-capable models can respond with text or audio, and the speech pipeline is a valid alternative.

questions.question: A company is building a voice assistant for phone calls. Callers must be able to interrupt the assistant while it is speaking, with minimal latency. Which approach should you recommend?

options.text: A realtime model or the Voice Live API
options.why: Correct. Realtime approaches stream audio in both directions with low latency and support interruptions.

options.text: Batch transcription followed by a text model
options.why: Batch transcription is asynchronous and unsuitable for live calls.

options.text: A Global Batch deployment of a chat model
options.why: Batch deployments have a target turnaround of up to 24 hours.
Sentiment analysis does not hold a voice conversation.

questions.explanation: Live, interruptible voice conversations use realtime models or the Voice Live API.
